page.overview:
What is Marish?

The Marish was the name of a fertile, yet boggy region located in the Eastfarthing of The Shire, across the Brandywine River from Buckland.

The Marish was an area of marshland reclaimed into farmland, located on the western banks of the River Brandywine. Its main settlements were the town of Stock in the north, the smaller village of Rushey in the center, and Deephallow in the south, which were all connected by the Causeway that traversed the Marish. A road, possibly the Stock Road, circled around its northern end, and the Stock-brook flowed through the region.

Much of the Marish was especially difficult to traverse, being full of bogs, ditches, briars, and fences. However, the eastern part of the landscape shifted into well maintained fields and meadows, drained using hedges, dikes, and gates. Between Stock and Rushey was the lane that led to Bamfurlong, the home of Farmer Maggot, and five miles to the north of that was the road that led to the Bucklebury Ferry.

The Marish was occupied by Hobbits that came into the Shire later than other bands. These were mostly Stoors who arrived from the south near Dunland around thirty years after the founding of the Shire. The folk of the Marish originated the technique of building farm-houses and barns above the ground. This habit later spread across the Shire, becoming well established. Even into the late Third Age, inhabitants of this region were often nicknamed "house-dwellers".
